findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant scoping in document lookups
findings.body: When a caller requests an ID belonging to another tenant, or IDs are reused across tenants, `getDocument` no longer forwards the tenant identity and this predicate can return another tenant’s document. The removed `ctx.tenantId` argument and `{ tenantId, documentId }` predicate enforced the tenant boundary.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve or intentionally migrate the cache module
findings.body: Consumers importing `readCached` from `src/cache.ts` will now fail to resolve the module at compile time or runtime. No replacement or migration is included, so deleting it breaks the existing exported contract.

findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant scoping in document lookups
findings.body:
Requests no longer constrain queries by `ctx.tenantId`. In a multi-tenant database, requesting an ID belonging to another tenant—or a tenant-local ID duplicated across tenants—can return another tenant’s document.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Preserve the exported cache module
findings.body:
Deleting `src/cache.ts` breaks every existing TypeScript or JavaScript consumer importing `readCached` from that module with a compile-time or runtime module-not-found error; no replacement exists.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant scoping when loading documents
findings.body:
The query no longer includes `ctx.tenantId`, bypassing the tenant authorization boundary. A caller who supplies a document ID belonging to another tenant can retrieve that tenant’s document whenever `db.find({ documentId })` resolves it.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Keep `tenantId` in the database predicate
findings.body:
When many tenants reuse the same `documentId`, this query retrieves every matching tenant record instead of one tenant’s record. Result size, database I/O, and memory now scale with tenant count and can become unbounded for common IDs.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
